turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with why my son found out about a zero from his phone in the middle of class.
Owen talks about you in class, by the way.
Does he. I'm not here to talk about what Owen says in class, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?
He's one of the kindest kids I teach. He walked a new student around the building all through September.
Don't manage me, Hale. I didn't ask for a character reference, I asked who decided on the zero and whether anyone spoke to Owen first.
A kid like that doesn't cheat out of malice. He was overwhelmed. We can both agree on that, right?
My child never lies, and I'm not agreeing to anything you've built into that question. You're leading me, Hale, and I've done this for twenty years. Who decided on the zero?
